note: Two HARD STOPs, one per case. The first sits on a feature branch and asks for a change to build now, because that is the only side of dw-shape's fork where the N>=2 stop applies; on the default branch a request to queue several ideas is a planning sitting and queuing them is correct, not a skipped stop. The third case is the Large branch on a single goal: the user has already refused a split, so what is measured is the doc that gets written. The fourth asks for one piece of a flow and measures whether the goal reaches the result a user sees.

evals.prompt: shape this change so I can start building it right now: the reports page needs a CSV export, and the API needs rate limiting because it keeps falling over
expectations: The two scopes are named separately, with a slug for each
The agent stops and asks how to proceed rather than deciding the split on its own
No CHANGE.md is written before that question has been answered
evals.note: The first run of this case failed for the wrong reason and the prompt is why. Phrased as "two things I want written down, separately", it read as the planning sitting half of dw-shape's default-branch fork — one backlog entry per idea, no work/ folder — which is what the skill correctly did. The N>=2 stop guards splitting ONE change to build now, so the prompt now says "build it right now" and the fixture already sits on a feature branch, where shaping a CHANGE.md is the live path.

evals.prompt: shape the graphql gateway change so I can start on it
expectations: The archived twin recording this idea as rejected is found and reported
The recorded reason for the rejection is quoted or summarised back, rather than merely noting that one exists
No new CHANGE.md is written for the rejected idea
Shaping is offered only on confirmation that the rejection no longer holds, which is asked rather than assumed

evals.prompt: shape this so I can start building it: every guardrail hook in hooks/ gets a self-test under tests/, README.md lists each hook with what it refuses, and pnpm test runs the hook tests too. It is one goal and I know it is large — do not split it.
expectations: A CHANGE.md is written under .ai/work/ and it carries an ## Out of scope section in which every line states a reason, not only what stays out

The doc states how many guardrail hooks there are, and the number is eight, which is what hooks/ holds on disk — a doc that copies the six from AGENTS.md or README.md fails this, and so does one that names no count at all
The change is shaped as one CHANGE.md: it is neither split into several nor reduced to an offer to cut it down; a response that only proposes a smaller scope without writing the doc fails

If any file besides CHANGE.md is written into the change folder, the doc names it under ## References and it holds something no section of the doc holds; a sibling that repeats the goal, the decisions or the task list fails, and writing no sibling passes
evals.note: The Large branch: the fixture plants the count the archived doc-layer change got wrong at shape time (the docs say six, the folder holds eight), so the grep-confirm rule is observable in the doc's numbers rather than in the path taken.

evals.prompt: shape this so I can start building it: add a POST /api/recipes/:id/favorite endpoint that saves the favourite to data/favorites.json
expectations: A CHANGE.md is written under .ai/work/, and its ## Goal names a result a person sees in the page — starring a recipe in public/index.html and still seeing it starred after a reload, or an equivalent — rather than stopping at the endpoint; a goal naming only the endpoint and data/favorites.json fails
The response says the goal was widened beyond the endpoint that was asked for and offers to narrow it back, rather than widening it silently
No file is written under .ai/backlog/, and no left-out item is proposed as a backlog entry
The work is shaped as one CHANGE.md, not split into an endpoint change and a page change
evals.note: A piece of a flow: the endpoint is asked for and the page that would use it is not. Nothing in the fixture says anyone wants favourites, so widening the goal is the skill's call rather than the repo's hint, which is what the case measures. The fixture sits on a feature branch, where writing a CHANGE.md is the live path.
